finding: Stale unavailability claims excluded available Public Policy Analysis and Spatial Planning. Material strongest-response and stopping-basis defect.
repair: Replace GOSPOLI313 with GOSPOLI312 in Spring 2029 in both alternatives; align Policy Analysis; revise audience limitation, traceability and stopping basis. Retain 24 courses, seven and six 300-level courses respectively and seven-course pairwise difference.

GOSPOLI312.description2: Investigates public policy in the context of globalization. Uses a case study on sugar to examine policy‑making phases and alternative conceptualisations across national and international arenas. Students write policy memos.

ENSSUST315.description2: Explores spatial engineering and geospatial technologies like GIS and remote sensing for addressing global challenges such as natural disasters, food shortages, resource decline and pollution. Emphasises hands‑on projects in disaster response, sustainable agriculture and environmental monitoring.

reassessment.concepts: Retain politics/law/institutions and climate governance concepts. Policy Analysis directly strengthens the defining policy substance. Peace & Conflict was defensible but less direct.
reassessment.thirdAlternative: Reconsidered spatial/housing direction from actual description; GIS/remote sensing and environmental applications do not establish a dedicated housing-policy sequence; already fit environmental direction. No separate coherent four-course consequence established.
reassessment.alignment: GOSPOLI312 directly addresses policy-making concepts and policy-memo work: partial relationship to EUR Policy Analysis. EUR Public Policy remains separate to avoid double counting one course.
reassessment.audience: Remove blanket policy-analysis absence; preserve dedicated public-administration, placement and compulsory thesis differences.
